% [APP 3]
\begin{table}[tbp]
  \centering
  \small
  \caption{\textbf{What the cross-source comparison rests on, and how far to trust it.} Two questions, both of which are usually settled silently. \emph{First}, comparing base models of different depth needs a rule for pairing their layers, and the two defensible rules pick opposite ends of gemma: by block index PCFG's layers pair with gemma's L1 and L3, by relative depth $(L{+}1)/N$ with gemma's L6 and L12 and L18 and L24. Block index wins on the mean (8.8 points against 14.8), which is why it is what Figure~\ref{fig:cross-source-layer-response} draws---though the margin rests largely on one measure, and the reconstruction filter is inert on PCFG in any case. \emph{Second}, a small gap is only impressive if the measure could have been far apart. The last two columns ask that: \emph{range} is how far each measure moves across all 10 graded runs, and the ratio is the gap against it. The two readings do not agree---edges improving reconstruction is near the bottom on raw points and near the top on the ratio---so both are printed and neither is called correct. The honest summary is that the three measures with the smallest raw gaps are also the three pinned against a boundary ($\geq 2$ parents at 89--100\%, sibling redundancy at 3--6\%, the frequency control at 0--2\%), where agreement costs the two sources nothing. \textbf{On 2 shared layers none of this is a result.}}

% [APP 4]
\begin{table}[tbp]
  \centering
  \small
  \caption{\textbf{The rank rule's null depends on dictionary size.} $S_\mathrm{res}$ passes an edge when both decoders fall in the top $k = 5$ of the probe's correlations over the whole dictionary. It is a geometry test, so an unrelated parent passes whenever chance puts it there, at a rate of $k/D$. The same $k$ is therefore two orders of magnitude stricter on gemma than on a 42-feature toy, and a measured pass rate is only interpretable against its own null: two runs on the \emph{same} 1{,}792-latent dictionary land on opposite sides of theirs. Reporting $S_\mathrm{res}$ shares across sources without this correction compares nothing.}

% [APP 5]
\begin{table}[tbp]
  \centering
  \small
  \caption{\textbf{One contaminating token position moved five of six metrics.} Means over the 5 layers graded both before and after the fix, block pair B0$\rightarrow$B1, before and after excluding the beginning-of-sequence position. BOS is an attention sink on which effectively every feature fires; with 400 documents it gave every pair in the dictionary 400 joint firings against a support guard of $\mathrm{MIN\_JOINT} = 30$, so the guard admitted pairs that never co-occur anywhere else. Every quantity computed from that one co-firing matrix moved, and the one that is not --- a ratio over children that already have a parent --- did not. \textbf{The \emph{before} column is withdrawn} and is reproduced only to size the error. Agreement among detectors that share an input is much weaker evidence than a battery implies.}
  \label{tab:bos}
  \begin{tabular}{lrrrr}
